newsitem.title: USA: US Plains fed cattle light-moderate $64 - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: US Plains fed cattle light-moderate $64 - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle sales midday Friday were light to moderate at $64.00 per cwt, steady with this week's hefty movement, feedlot sources said.

About 18,400 head sold in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area following weekly movement of 94,100, USDA reported. About 500 steers and heifers sold in Kansas following weekly sales of 93,600 in Kansas.

Sales this week at $64.00 per cwt were $2.00 higher than last week's top, with gains tied to a number of factors including higher CME live cattle futures and escalating beef demand, the feedlot sources said.
Fairly active fed cattle sales also kept most feedlots current, with much of this week's showlists sold, they said.
Showlists next week were seen about steady, with owners pricing cattle at $65.00 to $66.00, cattle feeders said.
Beef prices at midday remained firm, with boxed beef cut-out values quoted up $0.42 to $0.62 per cwt, and 150 fabricated loads sold, USDA said.
Heavyweight choice beef was quoted at $101.42, up $0.51 from Thursday and up $2.38 since a week ago Thursday when prices turned higher, USDA statistics showed.
